content.label: Terrific product, very well designed, fairly expensive and you can see why. But there are around five locations you can enjoy for free if you can't afford the whole package. The only problem with that it places a desire to try the other places that feels like an obsession. That's how good the program is. Relax, stress release, meditate, breathe correctly, plus more. Amazing!

title.label: Great App! Very focused on core principle.

content.label: Portal is a great app for meditation and relaxation. It’s also great for productivity and focus. I enjoy the ambiance the app provides. Would be great if they had more features such as the ability to cast via AirPlay or a mini player on the iPad.

title.label: A subtle masterpiece of visual and audiable effects

content.label:
In my decades of wilderness travels, I've learned to appreciate the "pace" of scenic vistas -- in terms of their sounds, weather, and creature movements therein.  

Portal will make you feel "present" in beautifully curated scenic vistas while you work. 

Install Portal and select from among dozens of stunning scenic vistas for display on your desktop background.  Add headphones to "hear" them as well.  

Twenty minutes in, take a moment to clear your desktop and pause work for 5 minutes to look and listen carefully at Portal's scenic vista.   It is the moment when you discern a subtle "pace" -- of a spider's thread gently weaving itself in the breeze, a leaf falling, clouds slowly rising above glacial ice, sunlight movement through the mist etc -- THIS is what makes Portal's scenic vistas so magical and fresh through your day!

Portal artfully energizes my unconscious mind with subtle background visuals and audio effects while I work.   I am delighted to have found Portal!  With gratitude, my thanks goes to Stuart Chan and team!!

I dont think I have ever left a review for an app before but I love this apps concept. 

Suggestions for updates
- custom wallpaper & sound options
- option to choose different sounds for the default on the wallpaper.
- a way to see your favorites in the desktop app
- more nighttime options
- more lighting integration (maybe smartthings?)
- scroll arrows on the favorites in the menu bar app or make it scroll when you scroll up and down (I have laptop connected to dock and the mouse I use  doesnt scroll left-to-right without holding shift)
- a library of all the wallpapers in the desktop app so I can quickly go through testing them and marking my favorites without reading about the location or picking a mood.
- a way to choose different wallpapers for different displays
- a 360 degree video option if you want to setup screens on multiple walls to feel ultra-immersed or have a vr headset
-random wallpaper from favorites that changes daily or with the weather of your location

Thank you for making this app!!!

I just started using Portal to relax and it is great.  I had a headache in my eye and I used it to relax and take a nap in the middle of the day and it worked.  No headache and I am very relaxed.  Can't wait to use it tonight.

I do enjoy using portal and generally put it on most nights HOWEVER the cost isn’t particularly justifiable. There’s a nice handful of portal options but considering how infrequently there’s updates with new content it’s hard to not think about the millions of videos that exist on YouTube for free that match the experience.

title.label: Fantastic app but can be better

content.label: I really like this app, this app digs deep into the possibilities of dynamic wallpaper, with the sound is also very natural. But I need some extra feature, like hide the dock icon, randomly switch according to time, etc.
Zin Uru!!!!
Definitely exceeded my expectations. Maybe make it a true portal and add live cams one day?

I am in love with this app. I have just a few suggestions. First, please increase the quality of the sound. Spatial audio is nice but the water sounds like low bitrate white noise. Second, please make it possible to hide the app icon from the dock and only have it in the menu bar. Third, it would be awesome if the surrounding/wallpaper could be set to automatically change every few minutes. Lastly, it would be amazing to have this on the Apple TV (hint hint)!

title.label: Shockingly Expensive For What You Get

content.label:
$10/month for some video files looping audio. You even download this files, so it’s not like they have to pay for servers and bandwidth to steam it all. 

Not a particularly large number of options to choose from and very few new options added on a regular basis. 

Look… it’s a cool app. I don’t particularly like the UI from a functionality perspective, but it’s gorgeous and the locations are gorgeous. It could easily justify itself as a one-time purchase with upgrades for add-on packs.

I signed up for a much discounted annual subscription expecting lots of updates, but there hasn’t been much. I cancelled my subscription probably 10 months before its renewal date.

In short: cool app but nonsensical business model

The video and audio experience provided by Portal is absolutely beautiful and incredibly immersive. I use Portal throughout my day with my morning coffee, during work and while relaxing in the evening. The experience on Mac and iPad are my favorite due to the larger screens, but having Portal on iPhone is the perfect companion when on the go. Combining Portals’ spacial audio experience with AirPods Max or AirPods Pro is a definite treat!
subscription

I am using 2 external monitors - not sure if that is the reason.  I really want to purchase the app but it simply prevents me to have all my screens available to do my work. These little things kill my focus and bring my attention back to the video glitches.

title.label: Best app on the App Store for Mac.

content.label: Nothing so profoundly affects my daily routine as Portal does, both on iPhone and (most recently) on Mac. Phenomenal job on both platforms, guys! I can’t wait to see what’s in store for Portal and look forward to visiting more places around the world through this amazing app!
I’m about to go to bed but thought to review this app after using it for a year. I’m super happy with my purchase!

title.label: A Multitool for Your Mind - Pure Bliss!

content.label:
I am absolutely floored by this app! Picture a Swiss Army knife, but instead of being for physical needs, it's designed for rejuvenating the mind and soul. This app is a masterfully crafted gateway to the world's most breathtaking natural vistas, regardless of where you physically might be.

The audio is a standout feature for me - the natural sounds are so immersive, you can almost feel the ocean spray or the grass beneath your feet. It's a transformative experience that takes you straight out of your typical environment and into the heart of nature. Best of all, the organic symphony of nature is evergreen. 

In conclusion, I cannot recommend this app enough. It's a necessity for anyone looking to spruce up their productivity and bring a bit of nature's magic into their everyday tasks!

Portal is a great app to really help with focusing on tasks by minimizing the distactions that are inherent with working on computers. By removing or reducing the distration of busy desktops, notifications, system sounds, etc., portal does a great job creating a viaul and auditory atmosphere that is conducive for productivity and peace. The UI is stunning!

title.label: High Quality images and sound (and very soothing!)

I would love!

title.label: Fantastic and wonderful will only grow more so

content.label: I have to go 5 stars I have suggestions but the overall effect is it’s displaced much of my other music listening and ‘white noise’ sleep machine use. Overall currently there is a trend towards steady sounds for relaxation sleep and focus and fewer that make me feel more awake and feel a bright sunny day (like the cows of Slovenia!). The Scottish locales are fantastic along with brooks, the winters mountains and wind awesome. It’s a bit of a learning curve what to navigate (check out the faqs I learned that sleep mode isn’t just certain portals it’s a MODE as are the others), and as above some perhaps ‘activating’ (bright sky something motor than continuous sound but not distracting jars of surprise obviously. The rustling barely field is another good one.  I also very much enjoy the smart nightjar integration and had a ‘oooooh’ moment changing to the fireplace and having my light go from some glue to amber flames! Looking forward to playing around getting it on bigger screens and seeing what happens with the range of dynamics in portals as they come up. Clearly some are the favorites but I suspect it’s hard to predict until they make it and see. Shirt of my one fav streaming music app possibly the best yearly subscription (and much less $!) I’ve spent!!

I rarely write reviews, but I absolutely love this app and had to give my feedback.  I’ve looked long and hard for nature scenes that can just fill my phone screen while I’m working in the office or just looking to escape the regular daily routine.  This app is awesome in that way.  It gives you the ability to feel like you’ve entered into a spot of the world just for you.  If there was one critique I could give, I’d like the scenes to be a little longer, they refresh in a few minutes (doesn’t stop soundscape or anything) it would just feel like more of an adventure if you could walk through the forest etc.  regardless, amazing app.

Any plans for Apple TV and Apple Watch apps? Also just a suggestion, wish for thunderstorm portals my hue lights would flash then hear the thunder just like another app called Thunderscapes unless you guys can’t use that same idea. Otherwise, great app and looking forward to future updates

The best for relaxing. The best for study. The best for quiet time. Simply the best.

title.label: Shrill birds break my brain and other issues

content.label:
Almost loved it, but birds are loud, shrill and not relaxing. In all portals w birds, they are  not balanced w other frequencies for proportional, non-hearing loss atmosphere. This occurs when listening across different devices / settings, but worst in headphones. Like ice pick piercing thru center of my brain. Maybe include equaliser or mixer for user customisation?

Not much appealing ab starter package due to “immersive” = great for ppl w hearing loss, so I am just disappointed bc i REALLY love the concept, the aesthetic, features…

Oh yeah, except the alarm clock is half functional. That was the big feature i was looking forward to trying. The 24 hour clock option is a fail: setting alarm and display always show am/pm no matter my selection. Also, no way to sample the backup alarm choices: “singing bowls” or “morning (whatever its called)”…i know i will need it to wake me sooner or later, so i need to make sure it is a sound at a volume sufficient to do so. That’s just weird and seems like a bug (that it won’t play sample). So the features? They could be great, one day….

🫶the freebie to Ukraine 🇺🇦. Definitely get a star just for that. 

Basically, feels like work in progress though it looks exquisite in presentation / at first glance. Free version needs beefing up for those of us who are not rich and can’t scrape together $10/mo (or other pricing options) for what amounts to *better than average but not great* sound samples, pretty pictures, and some handy features that aren’t quite functional. The paid content library is mostly variations on the 3 typical themes: bodies of water sounds, precipitation sounds, and outdoor creatures (birds/crickets/frogs/etc). 

I will be honest and reiterate: I'm bitter bc i really wanted this app to work for me, and all the more bummed bc it doesn't. Frankly, I know that’s a tall order, so I am definitely rooting for improvements and success for the whole enterprise + it’s creators.
Don’t expect it to change my life, but it’s definitely higher quality than most nature sounds apps.
I use the Portal app to focus on to relax. It helps me get through my day some days. Especially if I’m really stressed for work.
There are many apps that do similar things to this app but none do it better than Portal and it’s just that simple 🤷‍♂️
